Subject: POC trial success criteria & next steps - Atlas Payments

Thanks again for the time this morning, Aiden — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we’re aligned before the kickoff:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: real-time payments routing assistant (fraud detection support + routing suggestions) integrated into Ops console.
- Expected load: ~150–250 requests/sec during peak, average payload ~350 tokens.
- Key constraints: P95 latency < 300ms, sustained throughput >= 200 TPS for batch/streaming endpoints, cost target <= $0.0008/token to keep unit economics stable.
- Quality target: intent match >= 90% on validation set; acceptable hallucination rate < 2%.

Proposed POC scope (3 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, sandbox API keys, dataset exchange, access to test environment.
- Week 1: integration and baseline runs (latency/throughput baseline, end-to-end validation).
- Week 2: stress/load tests and cache/batching tuning; run cost-estimation scenarios.
- Week 3: evaluation against the rubric, final report, decision meeting.

Success criteria we propose to measure (please confirm)
- Latency: P95 < 300ms for 95% of requests in peak workload.
- Throughput: sustain >= 200 TPS with tail-latency SLOs met.
- Cost: effective cost <= $0.0008/token under expected batch sizes.
- Quality: intent match >= 90% on the provided eval set; F1/accuracy as discussed.

Ownership
- Redwood: Jordan (commercial/coordination) + Marissa (solutions lead, integration/tests).
- Atlas: Aiden (product owner) + Sofia (procurement/PO).

Next steps
1) Aiden — confirm the success criteria above or flag changes by EOD Mon.
2) Jordan/Marissa — schedule kickoff for Tue or Wed next week; share preliminary POC scope doc (attached).
3) Atlas — share test dataset and any sample traffic patterns + sandbox credentials.

Attachments: POC_Scope_v1.pdf (scope & timeline)
Links: evaluation template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_eval_sheet

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

—
Jordan Blake

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the main points and a couple of adjustments from our side:

- Success criteria: All look good. Small tweaks: target cost preferably <= $0.00075/token if possible (we'll accept $0.0008 as a stretch), and we'd like to measure 99th percentile latency (not just P95) for some critical flows — target 99th < 500ms.
- Throughput: 200 TPS is correct for peak; we may see short spikes to 300 TPS for <5 minutes — please include spike behavior in the load plan.

We can provide a representative eval set (~5k labeled messages) and sample traffic traces by COB Monday. Sofia will handle PO timeline — she’s looped.

Quick scheduling: Tue 9am PT kickoff works for us. Can Marissa lead the technical agenda?

Thanks,
Aiden

Thanks Jordan and Aiden — appreciate the clarity. I’ve attached a lightweight test plan and the evaluation template to this thread (see attachments). High-level technical plan below:

Technical plan summary
- Week 1 (integration): validate auth, run single-client baseline for latency; capture p50/p95/p99 and token counts.
- Week 2 (load & tuning): run controlled ramp to 300TPS for short bursts (5min), sustained 200TPS for 30min to validate autoscaling and batching; enable KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Week 3 (eval): run customer eval set (5k labeled messages) against production variant and tuned variant; produce confusion matrix, F1, precision/recall, and hallucination audit.

Measurement & reporting
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 reported per endpoint; use 10s buckets for spike analysis.
- Throughput: sustained TPS, success rate, and tail-error rates.
- Cost: tokenized cost analysis per run; modeled under expected batch sizes and caching.
- Quality: intent-match percent, F1, and hallucination sample rate (manual spot-check of 200 responses).

Attachments included (stubs):
- evaluation_template.xlsx (evaluation metrics + rubric)
- POC_Scope_v1.pdf (timeline & responsibilities)

Action items

- Sofia: confirm PO cadence/any procurement timing constraints.
- Jordan: please send the calendar invite for Tue 9am PT (kickoff).

I’ll run the technical agenda and share the test-run scripts after kickoff. If anything else needs updating on the success criteria, flag it in the invite.
